title: Match Expression
concept: match is like a super-powered if — it compares a value against multiple patterns and runs the first matching arm.
why: match is cleaner and safer than chains of if/elif for multi-way branching. The compiler checks you've covered all cases.
tips: `match` is exhaustive — every possible value must be handled (or use `_`)
Patterns are checked from top to bottom — order matters!
All arms must return the same type — like if-expression
Use `match` for value-based branching, `if` for condition-based branching
common_mistakes: Forgetting the `_` wildcard — match must be exhaustive
Using `match` for simple true/false checks where `if` is clearer
Arms returning different types — they must all be the same type
